subject: Post-incident log sweep — clearance & evidence package
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Morgan <lisa.morgan@atlasbank.com>; AtlasBank Security <security@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T09:17:00Z
Subject: Post-incident log sweep — clearance & immediate next steps

Hi Lisa / AtlasBank security team,

Following the outage window we discussed this morning, our internal incident response team completed a directed log sweep across the serving fleet and control plane. High-level summary up front: we found no activity indicating unauthorized exfiltration, and no read operations against customer data stores outside expected service flows.

What we did:
- Collected host and application logs across affected nodes (ingest, runtime, and routing) for the 24-hour window surrounding the incident.
- Replayed access logs against S3-like storage and internal blob store to confirm object-level access patterns.
- Cross-checked RBAC audit trails and API key usage against the customer routing policies.

Initial findings:
- No successful outbound transfers to external IPs beyond our documented egress endpoints.
- No anomalous API key usage tied to AtlasBank identifiers.
- KV cache audits show standard eviction/refresh events; no cache-dump operations were present.

Requested next steps from your side: please let us know if you want the full exported artifacts for independent review. We can provide a redacted artifact set and a checklist of verification steps your security team can run.

I'll loop Hannah and Marcus in for the evidence package — they will attach the exports and a short technical memo.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

[Attachment stub: redwood_log_export_20270428.zip (log export, 73MB)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Morgan <lisa.morgan@atlasbank.com>, AtlasBank Security <security@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-incident log sweep — clearance & immediate next steps

Lisa — attaching the evidence package and a short audit summary as requested. Key points in the attached audit_summary_20270428.csv: request timestamps, source IPs, request paths, API key hash (truncated), and a disposition column where we flagged anything that required follow-up (none flagged for AtlasBank).

Technical notes (short):
- We exported the following artifacts for your review:
  - application_access.log (rotated, gzipped)
  - egress_flow.log (network flow samples)
  - kvcache_inspect.csv (cache keys scanned for TTL/ops)
  - rbac_audit.log (policy evaluation traces)
- We validated checksums for each exported file and included checksum.txt in the archive.
- For privacy, customer identifiers were left intact for AtlasBank per your sharing agreement; we can further redact if you'd like an anonymized copy.

Attached: redwood_log_export_20270428.zip, audit_summary_20270428.csv, kvcache_retention_notes.pdf

If you want an interactive walk-through of the export, Marcus can join to explain the kvcache inspection and what the lifecycle events mean.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Security Engineer, Incident Response | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

[Attachment stubs: audit_summary_20270428.csv (5KB), kvcache_retention_notes.pdf (12KB), redwood_log_export_20270428.zip (73MB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: AtlasBank Security <security@atlasbank.com>, Lisa Morgan <lisa.morgan@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-incident log sweep — clearance & immediate next steps

Hi team — quick technical addendum to explain why we consider the KV cache behaviour clean:

- The runtime maintains an in-memory KV cache for tokenizer/prompts and a separate persistent blob index for model artifacts. During the incident window we observed no cache snapshot or export API calls in the audit trail. The only writes were standard eviction/refresh cycles driven by usage.
- We instrumented a one-off consistency scan that hashes live cache keys against a projection from the prior 72-hour window; the hash deltas matched expected churn.
- Network telemetry shows no sustained outbound TCP connections from worker nodes to unknown destinations; egress was limited to our manifest endpoints (listed in the attached summary).

If your security reviewers want to validate the checksums, we included SHA256 values in checksum.txt inside the zip. Happy to run a screen-share and walk through the export verification.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

[Attachment reference: kvcache_retention_notes.pdf included in prior message]

From: Lisa Morgan <lisa.morgan@atlasbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasBank Security <security@atlasbank.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-incident log sweep — clearance & immediate next steps

Jordan / Hannah / Marcus — thank you for the fast turnaround and the detailed package. We ran a quick checksum validation and spot-checked traces; the artifacts look consistent with your findings. Our security team appreciates the granularity on KV cache and egress endpoints.

Next items for documentation:
- We will close the active support ticket after we receive a short statement from Redwood confirming that no AtlasBank data was exfiltrated during the incident. The statement can be informal but should reference the artifacts provided (audit_summary_20270428.csv and redwood_log_export_20270428.zip).
- Please include the JIRA INF-9876 link in your closure note.

Can you supply that by EOD tomorrow? Once we have it we can mark the incident as resolved on our side.

Regards,

Lisa Morgan
Senior InfoSec Manager | AtlasBank
